Yes, maybe let me take you through the ones you're referencing, and then you can kind of ask further questions. First, advanced packaging. We're very excited about what's going on with advanced packaging. You hear people in the industry talk about chiplet architecture, dye disaggregation, high bandwidth memory uses, I call it advanced packaging. But through silicon via to put the 8 DRAM die together. This is great business for Lam. If you think about to do the advanced packaging stuff, you're stacking things on top of other things, you're interconnecting things. Generally speaking that means you're depositing conductive material, to create the electron path and you're having to etch things, to open up the room to put the conductive material down. That's what we do. And so when you look at this, I guess if we started the year we were suggesting, hi, in a couple of years' time this will be $1 billion business for us, the advanced packaging in total. Then as the year progressed we said, hi, it's $1 billion this year. And then more recently we said it's actually more than $1 billion this year. So this is a great inflection. It's going to keep growing for the foreseeable future, right. If you look at high bandwidth memory, HBM3 is going to 3E. So 8 DRAM die going to 12. 3E will go to 4, so 12 will go to 16. That's more interconnect, right. It's more equipment capacity is ramping for that, so there's that. And like I said, all of the chiplet architecture that you hear the CPU guys and the GPU guys talk about, we enable a lot of that with the TSV process, we are very strong in those applications. So anyway, excited about that. It's more than $1 billion this year and growing into next year. So that's the first one. The second one that we've been talking about is gate-all-around. And again, I like billion dollar numbers. We like billion dollar numbers. And so the quantification for that for us, is when you look at the gate-all-around structure, it is very etch and deposition intensive. To create those sheet architecture, you're depositing films, you're selectively etching them. The intensity of etch and deposition grows to the tune of $1 billion addressable market for every 100,000 wafer starts at capacity that gets put in place. So we're excited about that obviously that's incremental opportunity. Now we're not going to get 100% market share there. As much as we would love to do that, that just doesn't happen in this industry. But we're going to do well there. And so that's an incremental opportunity that ramps into next year. We have said actually that the investment for the whole node, the whole gate-all-around node this year, not just the creation of the sheets, is $1 billion in revenue this year that counts. So just to kind of get your head wrapped around that and growing into next year, obviously. The next one, and again it's another billion dollar number is backside power. And that one likely is late next year, maybe into '26. But that also when we look at the intensity of depositing, metallization and etching, the structure is another billion dollar incremental opportunity, for etch and deposition for every 100,000 wafer starts of capacity that gets put in place. So obviously, we're excited about these things, because when you look at the evolution of architectures, they're moving in the third dimension. They're more materials intensive. And that plays to the strength of the things we do. We deposit film on silicon wafers and we etch them. So then a little bit further down the road, we've been talking about this for a while is dry photoresist where we are collaborating with ASML, to put the resist down in a dry fashion. It enables the photons from the EUV tool to more effectively be absorbed and creates efficiency as a result of that. That's a little bit further away, but I can see in four, five years' time, that also will be a $1 billion opportunity for us. So when we look at these things, we're innovating. We're evolving to grow incremental opportunities that we see, because of the evolution of where the industry is going.
